data.name: Balbhadra
data.long_meaning: Balbhadra is a Sanskrit name derived from two roots: 'Bal' meaning power and 'Bhadra' meaning generous. This name is attributed to Lord Vishnu, who is revered for his immense power and his generous nature towards his devotees.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that invokes blessings of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing power, generosity, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Balbhadra, also known as Balavadra, was a king of the Vatsa dynasty, which ruled over the region of Magadha in ancient India, around 365-338 BC. He was a contemporary and ally of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Magadha region, Vatsa dynasty, contemporary and ally of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya

historical_references.reference: Balbhadra was also a general in the army of the Satavahana king Gautamiputra Satakarni, who ruled over the Deccan plateau in southern India, around 130-158 AD. Balbhadra is best known for his victory over the Shaka invader Rudradaman I at the Battle of Kalinga.
